s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abnormal posturing and movement disorder following medication change
salient_findings: Bouts of extremely stiff, nonpainful neck that tilted her head involuntarily leftwards, upwards, and backwards in hyperextension
Conjugate deviation of the eyes upward or laterally
Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
key_facts: 19-year-old female student
Admitted with grade III dyspnea
Prescribed diuretics and aspirin post-surgery
Started a new medication at low dose (25 mg per day) for two days
Dose was increased to 25 mg twice daily on the third day
Readmitted on the same evening after discharge on the fifth postoperative day
Subpulmonic ventricular septal defect
Severe aortic regurgitation due to right coronary cusp prolapse
Dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 40%
Mild aortic regurgitation on post-repair transesophageal echocardiographic assessment
Blood chemistry and electrolyte levels were within normal limits

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of an extremely stiff, nonpainful neck, conjugate deviation of the eyes, and involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward are consistent with an acute dystonic reaction, which can be triggered by certain medications, especially after a recent increase in dose.

rejected.label: Tardive Dyskinesia
rejected.why: Tardive dyskinesia typically occurs after long-term use of antipsychotic medications, which is not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Drug-Induced Parkinsonism
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the typical parkinsonian features such as tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia.

rejected.label: Antipsychotic-Induced Dystonia
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient being on antipsychotic medication, making this option less likely.

rejected.label: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor-Induced Dystonia
rejected.why: The new medication started by the patient is not specified as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, making this option less likely without further information.
